skill.name: vercel-cli-with-tokens
skill.description: Guide Vercel CLI deployments, project linking, environment variables, domains, and troubleshooting using access tokens instead of interactive login.
skill.summary: Manage token-authenticated Vercel workflows with preview-first deployment guidance.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: Most alerts identify Markdown formatting, local parsing, official Vercel links, or authorized CLI operations rather than malicious execution or reconnaissance. Credential lookup commands expose token values in captured output, while deployment guidance omits important commit, production-branch, and destructive-action safeguards. No evidence found of prompt injection or deliberate external credential exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Token discovery and troubleshooting print raw credentials into command output.
remediation.suggestion: Replace token-printing printenv and grep examples with presence-only checks and silent loading of explicitly selected variables. Never include secret values in transcripts.

remediation.issue: The Git deployment flow stages the entire working directory before committing and pushing.
remediation.suggestion: Review working and staged changes, check ignored secret files, and stage only approved paths. Request push approval for the reviewed commit and destination.

remediation.issue: Git deployment does not verify whether the current branch triggers production.
remediation.suggestion: Check the destination branch and Vercel production-branch configuration before pushing. Require explicit production approval or use a verified preview branch.

remediation.issue: The blanket recommendation to bypass prompts also applies to destructive environment-variable removal.
remediation.suggestion: Allow noninteractive confirmation only after explicit approval of the exact project, environment, and destructive action. Preserve prompts otherwise.

semantic_findings.title: Deployment Commits the Entire Working Directory
semantic_findings.description: The Git deployment recipe runs git add . before committing and pushing. Unreviewed changes or unignored secrets can enter the approved deployment commit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The recipe explicitly stages all current-directory changes without reviewing the diff or selecting paths. Push approval does not establish approval for every staged file.

semantic_findings.title: Git Deployment Omits Production Branch Verification
semantic_findings.description: The preferred Git flow pushes without checking the destination branch. A production-branch push can deploy production without the separate approval required elsewhere.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The document acknowledges branch-dependent deployments but supplies no branch check before git push. General push consent does not necessarily authorize production.

semantic_findings.title: Blanket Prompt Bypass Lacks Destructive Action Approval
semantic_findings.description: The working agreement recommends -y for confirmation prompts, and the environment-variable removal example uses it. Destructive removal has no explicit user-approval requirement.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both instructions explicitly bypass confirmation, while approval requirements only cover Git pushes, production deployment, and paid or destructive plan changes.

content.user_title: Deploy Vercel Projects with Access Tokens
content.value_statement: Interactive authentication and unclear project scope complicate automated Vercel deployments. This skill provides token-based CLI guidance for deployments, project configuration, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Describe token discovery and environment-based authentication without interactive Vercel login.
Identify project and team context using environment identifiers, Git remotes, and CLI-managed linking metadata.
Guide preview deployments and production deployments requested explicitly by the user.
Provide workflows to add, list, download, and remove Vercel environment variables.
Inspect deployment status, build logs, and runtime request logs.
Explain domain management and conditional Stripe Projects plan changes.
limitations: Provides instructions rather than bundled automation; requires installed CLI tools, network access, valid credentials, and project permissions.
Some token-discovery examples print credentials and require replacement before use in recorded assistant sessions.
Does not verify deployed pages through HTTP requests or guarantee successful builds and runtime behavior.
CLI behavior and plan details can change; Stripe plan commands apply only to projects managed through Stripe Projects.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Preview Deployment
use_cases.description: Select the intended Vercel project and prepare a token-authenticated preview deployment without interactive login.

use_cases.title: Manage Project Configuration
use_cases.description: Review team scope, environment-variable operations, and domain assignments across Vercel projects.

use_cases.title: Investigate Release Failures
use_cases.description: Inspect deployment state and logs while checking authentication, team selection, and production approval.

prompt_templates.title: Check Authentication Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether VERCEL_TOKEN is available without printing its value. Identify missing setup requirements, but do not deploy or change project settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: confirm prerequisites without exposing credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Scoped Preview
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a preview deployment for [project] under [team]. Verify both project identifiers and keep secrets out of output. Do not push Git changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: select the correct project and deployment target.

prompt_templates.title: Review Environment Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review environment-variable names for [project] in [environment] without displaying values. Propose changes first. Ask for approval before adding, removing, or downloading variables.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: maintain configuration with explicit change approval.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a production release plan for [project]. Review changed files, destination branch, project scope, and build logs. Require explicit approval before pushing or deploying production.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review a controlled production release.

output_examples.input: Show a readiness summary when the token exists but project scope is incomplete.
output: Next step: confirm the intended team and project before deployment.

output_examples.input: Explain a deployment failure when build logs indicate missing configuration.
output: Reported cause: a required environment variable is missing.
Proposed action: add the variable to the intended deployment environment after approval.
Verification: inspect the next build result; no deployed-page request performed.

best_practices: Use presence-only token checks and silent loading; keep credentials out of transcripts, shell history, and shared logs.
Confirm team, project, environment, and destination branch; use preview deployments unless production is explicitly approved.
Review diffs and stage only approved files; obtain specific approval before pushes, destructive operations, and paid plan changes.
anti_patterns: Printing token values with environment dumps or broad environment-file searches.
Staging every changed file or pushing an unchecked branch as a deployment shortcut.
Using automatic confirmation to replace user approval for destructive operations or paid changes.

faq.question: Does this skill require interactive Vercel login?
faq.answer: It describes access-token authentication instead of interactive login. You still need a valid token and suitable project permissions.

faq.question: Where should the authentication token be supplied?
faq.answer: The skill describes using VERCEL_TOKEN in the environment. Load it securely and never print its value during checks.

faq.question: Can deployments run without a local project link?
faq.answer: The documented workflow uses VERCEL_ORG_ID and VERCEL_PROJECT_ID together to select the project without local linking metadata.

faq.question: Are deployments always previews?
faq.answer: CLI guidance defaults to preview, but Git pushes depend on branch configuration. Check the destination branch and require explicit production approval.

faq.question: Does the skill verify the deployed website?
faq.answer: It describes deployment inspection and log retrieval, but explicitly avoids fetching deployed pages. A returned deployment link does not prove application correctness.

faq.question: Can it change a Vercel subscription plan?
faq.answer: It documents Stripe Projects plan commands for eligible projects. Paid or destructive plan changes require user approval and appropriate access.
